summary.title: Threat model - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: Threat modeling is a process for finding and ranking potential threats to a system and choosing controls, and this page traces its history and lists common methods (STRIDE, PASTA, hybrid) and tools.
keywords: process for attack simulation and threat analysis
how to find threats to a system
takeaways: Threat modeling identifies potential threats such as structural vulnerabilities or missing safeguards, then prioritizes countermeasures.
Key history: attack trees (Schneier, 1998), STRIDE (Microsoft, 1999), OCTAVE (2003), and the Threat Modeling Manifesto (2020).
STRIDE covers Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege.
Most approaches start by drawing a data flow diagram, decomposing the system into elements, then checking each entry point against threat categories.
Tools named include Microsoft's Threat Modeling Tool, IriusRisk, securiCAD, SD Elements, OWASP Threat Dragon and OWASP pytm; threat modeling is also applied to vehicles and building automation.
summary.summary: This Wikipedia article defines threat modeling and gives its history, from early attack trees and threat trees through Microsoft's STRIDE and the 2020 Threat Modeling Manifesto. It then describes the main methodologies, including STRIDE, PASTA and a hybrid method, and explains the common process of building data flow diagrams and checking threats against categories. It closes with a list of commercial and open-source tools and notes on use in automotive and building automation.
